clue.text: Forceful doctor restraining macho types

indicators.note: restraining means holding something in, so the doctor word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor
he-men are macho, muscular types

explanation.surface: A forceful physician holds back some aggressive tough guys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restraining' signals the container; 'macho types' suggests a description of the doctor's patients, but it is the piece held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement words or actions are delivered with great force and passion, so forceful is a synonym.

clue.text: One that grips shows weakness

definitions.meaning: a clamp holding work on a bench, spelt vise in American usage
a moral failing or bad habit

explanation.surface: A tight grip reveals a flaw in character.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice is a bench clamp that grips work, and also a moral failing or weakness.

clue.text: Play card and ruin family

parts.note: a heart is a playing card of that suit
to break is to ruin
a house is a family line, as the House of Windsor

explanation.surface: A card game ruins family life.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartbreak House is a play by George Bernard Shaw, first staged in 1920.

clue.text: Obsession to be shortly in sparsely-populated province

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these pieces go inside the obsession word

parts.note: mania means an obsession
taken as written

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, losing a final letter

explanation.surface: A craving to be in an empty, remote region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' trims the last letter from 'be', and 'in' places the result together with 'to' within the obsession word.
explanation.definitionFit: Manitoba is a Canadian prairie province with a small population for its large area.

clue.text: Hot, without water going over Welsh town

indicators.note: in a down clue going over means placed above, so this piece comes first

parts.note: a neat drink is taken with no water added
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Hot and dry conditions pass over a town in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Neath is a town in south Wales, near Swansea.

clue.text: No end to advance warning?

definitions.meaning: to tip something off is to take its tip, its end, away, so it has no end left
a hint or warning given beforehand, as to the police

explanation.surface: Someone frets that advance warnings never stop coming.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip-off is an informal private warning given in advance; read literally, the phrase means removing the end.

clue.text: Demand contribution from twin sister

indicators.note: contribution from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone demands that their twin sister chip in.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to demand firmly, refusing to accept a no.

clue.text: Alas, store is empty —- nag for software

indicators.note: alas is a cry of dismay at things going wrong, telling us the words that follow are in a mess

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lament that the shop has nothing left, and a complaint about computer programs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alas' is a weak but intended signal that STORE IS EMPTY NAG gets rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An operating system is the core software that runs a computer, such as Windows or Linux.

clue.text: Operate ignition for vehicle needed in emergency

definitions.meaning: to fire an engine is to start it, operating its ignition
a truck that rushes to put out blazes

explanation.surface: Someone starts the ignition of an emergency vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire engine is the emergency vehicle sent to fight fires; read as a phrase it means start a motor.

clue.text: Sad dope employed in factory

indicators.note: employed in means working inside, so the dope word goes within the factory word

parts.note: a plant is a factory
gen is slang for information, as is dope

explanation.surface: A gloomy drug user works in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests drugs, but it means inside information, GEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangent describes a loud mournful sound, so sad in tone.

clue.text: Post on the mountains in a defensive link-up

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, so the post word follows the mountain word

parts.note: a chain is a range of mountains
mail is the post, letters delivered

explanation.surface: Letters are sent to a mountain range as part of some military alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: Chainmail is armour made of interlinked metal rings, a protective covering literally built from links.

clue.text: Officer needs attention for unpleasant mark

parts.note: SM is the abbreviation for sergeant major, a military officer
to lend an ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: An officer demands that someone listen up about a nasty stain.
explanation.definitionFit: A smear is a dirty streak or smudge, a mark nobody wants on their clothing or reputation.

clue.text: A bird is busy

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A bird is described as being occupied.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at it is an idiom for being busy, hard at work on something.

clue.text: Conciliatory gesture that takes the palm

definitions.text: Conciliatory gesture that takes the palm

parts.words: Conciliatory gesture that takes the palm
parts.note: to take the palm usually means to win a prize, but here a peacemaking gesture literally takes hold of another person's palm

explanation.surface: A peace-making gesture is declared the winner.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping hands is a customary gesture of reconciliation, and it physically grips the other person's palm.

clue.text: Denounces drunk that's a little the worse for wear

definitions.text: a little the worse for wear

parts.note: to shop someone is slang for informing on them
oiled is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone informs on a drunk who looks rather dishevelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop-soiled goods are slightly damaged or faded from handling and display, a little worn.

clue.text: Cynical, having been swindled by firm

parts.note: hard means firm, solid
bitten is slang for cheated or swindled

explanation.surface: Someone became cynical after being cheated by a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' reads as a company in the surface, but it is the adjective, HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-bitten describes someone toughened and cynical through bitter experience.

clue.text: Stewed apricot left -—- it could be too hot

indicators.note: stewed fruit is cooked down into a mush, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A warning that stewed apricot could be served too hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropical weather is extremely hot and humid, like conditions near the equator.

clue.text: Fighter protecting new dynasty

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding as a shield, so the fighter word encloses the other

parts.note: a MiG is a Soviet-built fighter jet

explanation.surface: A warplane guards a newly founded ruling house.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ming were the imperial dynasty that ruled China from 1368 to 1644.

clue.text: Study river's liquid course

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
the Somme is a river in northern France

explanation.surface: Someone studies the course of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Consommé is a clear soup, a liquid course served at a meal.

clue.text: Page is to drive in carriage

parts.note: to ram something in is to drive it in by force

explanation.surface: A pageboy is told to drive a carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A pram is a baby carriage, short for perambulator.

clue.text: Pirate captain keeping away an hour, I can make music

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the pirate's name surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: Henry Morgan was a famous Welsh pirate captain
out means away, not at home
H is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: A buccaneer boasts of keeping away for an hour so he can play music.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Morgan was a 17th-century buccaneer; 'keeping' puts both the away word and the hour letter together inside his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica is a small instrument that makes music, and the clue lets it speak for itself in the first person.

clue.text: Figure in sky accepting son's prayer

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the figure in the sky encloses the son

parts.note: Orion is the constellation of the hunter, a figure in the night sky
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A heavenly figure receives a boy's prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Orison is an archaic or literary word for a prayer.

clue.text: Different reasons must be announced, or else

parts.note: other means different

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so what is heard is the reasons word

parts.note: whys are reasons, as in the whys and wherefores

explanation.surface: A speaker insists different reasons should be declared, or there will be trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise and or else are synonyms, both meaning if not, in a different case.

clue.text: Austen heroine half satisfied to become a six-footer

indicators.note: half means only the first half of the heroine's name is used

parts.note: Emma is the heroine of Jane Austen's novel of that name
met as in met a need, satisfied it

explanation.surface: A Jane Austen heroine is half satisfied to become a tall person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person; it is an insect, with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: An emmet is an old dialect word for an ant, an insect with six legs.

clue.text: Messy room a sign of fault in classical stream

parts.note: a sty is a filthy, untidy room, like a pigsty
a cross, X, is marked against a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A teacher finds an untidy room and a cross marked against a mistake in a classics lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: The Styx is the river of the underworld in Greek mythology, a stream from classical legend.

clue.text: Use pressure with stick?

definitions.meaning: to poke or push someone, or urge them on
a pointed rod used for driving cattle

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to push with a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: To prod is to poke or press, and a prod is a pointed stick used to poke animals.

clue.text: I may be taken in by very poor clipped old coin

indicators.note: taken in by means enclosed by the following piece, so the I goes inside it
clipped means with its tail cut off, losing its last letter

parts.note: lousy means very poor, dreadful

explanation.surface: Someone admits being fooled by a badly trimmed antique coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipped' takes the last letter off LOUSY to leave LOUS, and the I sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A louis was a gold coin of pre-revolutionary France, named after its kings.

clue.text: Former college graduates change round

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the change word goes around the graduates

parts.note: to alter is to change
MA is a Master of Arts graduate; two graduates give two of them

explanation.surface: Graduates of an old college bring in reforms.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma mater, Latin for nourishing mother, is the school or college one formerly attended.

clue.text: Governess expected girl to be back

parts.note: due means expected, as a train is due

indicators.note: to be back means this word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A governess was expecting a girl to return.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman acting as chaperone and governess to girls in a Spanish household.

clue.text: Waved, like some chosen schoolchildren?

definitions.meaning: fluttered out in the wind, as a flag or long hair does
divided into ability groups in British schools

explanation.surface: Pupils picked for a parade waved at the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Streaming is a British school practice of placing pupils in classes by ability.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner streamed when it flew out in the wind; pupils are streamed when sorted by ability.
